channel.title: DRP & Co. LLP Insights
channel.description: Articles on valuation, governance, regulatory and tax matters from DRP & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants, Pune.

item.title: HDFC Bank chose an outsider. What happens to the insider who was not chosen?
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Boards spend months choosing a successor and almost no time on the runner-up, who usually holds the institution's memory. Plan both outcomes before anything is announced.

item.title: Did Fairfax get IDBI Bank at a 10% discount? Why the screen price was the misleading number
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A 60.72% stake sold at Rs. 81 when the share closed near Rs. 90. With 5% public float, the screen price was the number to doubt. Questions to ask before valuing your own stake.

item.title: He admitted his limits, then won a Nobel: the delegation lesson for founders
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Francis Halzen called himself a reluctant leader, hired a project director and stayed with the science. Founders who hold every job grow the business to the size of their diary.

item.title: Rent the skill or own it: what TCS's Rs. 650 crore subcontractor bill says to mid-sized businesses
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: TCS kept a bigger bench and still raised subcontractor spend to 6.8% of revenue. With attrition at 13.3%, renting niche skills is a strategy. Renting in a panic is a bill.

item.title: When a relative's business ends an independent director's term: SEBI's 50 lakh test
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: An independent director of Indian Oil resigned 34 days after appointment over her son's dealership. The SEBI rule behind it, and what boards should check.

item.title: Three giants, one month, three leadership shocks
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Three leadership shocks at India's largest companies in a month. A ninety-day test for promoters, and succession as three handovers, not one.

item.title: No fraud, no dispute. The auditors resigned over the fee.
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A listed company's auditors resigned two years into a five-year term because the fee did not cover the work. The three things that happen when audit fees are pushed down.

item.title: A valuation from July 2024, a vote in October 2026
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A merger exchange ratio is being voted on 26 months after its valuation date. Nothing improper, but a valuation is a photograph and relative value drifts.

item.title: One grandmaster in 1988, ninety-nine by 2026
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Anand did not build Indian chess. He removed a doubt. What the first person in any family, firm or town does for everyone behind them.

item.title: Two years of notice, thirty-five days to collapse
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: India's largest airline cancelled 4,500 flights after pilot rest rules it had known about for two years. Over-optimisation removed the slack. Where to keep yours.

item.title: The title deeds were missing. That was the whole story.
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A listed company's assets were pledged for its promoters' borrowings and nothing moved in the accounts. Three questions for every board's agenda this year.

item.title: The cheapest valuation is about to get expensive
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A Bill before Parliament would make IBBI the single valuation authority, with suspension of up to ten years. What that does to how valuers work and quote.

item.title: He wanted a new market. He needed a spreadsheet.
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Three weeks of product and customer profitability work showed the largest customer barely broke even. The highest return work is usually the boring work.

item.title: Their biggest customer was a country. It repriced overnight.
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A 50% US tariff froze Rs. 3,000 crore of Tirupur orders. The exporters who came through had built second doors years earlier. Find your 30% dependency.

item.title: The error was survivable. The fifteen months were not.
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A listed bank's accounting discrepancy cost 27% in a day. The regulator's order was about the fifteen-month gap before disclosure, and the two switches nobody flipped.

item.title: Investment value versus market value: Rs. 350 crore and Rs. 1,400 crore
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A DCF supported Rs. 350 crore; a strategic buyer's number crossed Rs. 1,400 crore. Neither was wrong. The gap is arithmetic, and it belongs to one buyer.

item.title: The most expensive way to learn is alone
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: The costliest mistakes of a career happen in the first few years and never feel like mistakes. A mentor is borrowed scar tissue. How to find one, and how to ask.

item.title: Same capital, same industry, 3% versus 15% margins
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Two chemical promoters an hour apart. One built for volume and owns a factory; the other built a niche and owns a market. Pricing power is what you own.

item.title: Kodak's biggest competitor worked in Kodak's own lab
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Kodak and Blockbuster both ran diligent competitor analysis. The threat that ended them never qualified for the slide. The question boards should ask instead.

item.title: EBITDA assumes your machines maintain themselves
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Two cement companies at 11 times EBITDA were a third apart in value once maintenance capex was counted. When to look at EV/EBIT instead.

item.title: Twenty decisions for a lifetime: Buffett's punch card for promoters
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Buffett's twenty-slot card is a lens, not a rule. The promoters in most trouble rarely made one bad decision; they made forty average ones.

item.title: The CFO who called the bank first survived
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Two logistics companies hit the same covenant breach. One CFO called the bank before it found out. With recovery rates doubled, silence no longer buys time.

item.title: The Rs. 40 crore related party lease that took three minutes to approve
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: A warehouse lease from the promoter's family came up for routine renewal. One independent director asked for the arm's length valuation. The rent was 22% above market.

item.title: The Supreme Court was asked to value Tata Sons shares. It refused.
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: SP Group said Rs. 1.75 lakh crore, Tata Sons said Rs. 70,000 to 80,000 crore. The Court declined to pick a number. What valuers and promoters should take from that.

item.title: What Bill Gates's Think Week says about a founder's calendar
item.dc:creator: CA Dhananjay Walke
item.description: Twice a year Gates disappears for seven days to think. Most founders fill every hour; the best thinking happens when there are no meetings at all.
